parsed.attack: Kill line four concedes the acquisition problem: it asks only that 100 of the first 1,000 sign-ups come from temples, gurdwaras or family chats, which means 90% are planned to come from paid placement. At a UK education-category CPI of $3-6 and category-standard ~3% conversion that is $100-200 per paying user, for a heritage-language app priced around GBP 3.99 ($5, below the $8-24 median payer) whose own kill line accepts 25% day-30 retention - a payer lasting 4-6 months returns $20-30 gross, $14-21 net. That is a 5-14x hole. The base caps it too: British Punjabi and Gujarati adults in their twenties and thirties number on the order of 300k, so 100% of them at 3% conversion is under 10,000 payers.
parsed.strongest_defence: On-device inference makes marginal cost zero, so the 10% community share is 100% margin and the 90% paid share is a planning assumption rather than a requirement; a grandmother's own recorded voice is a gift-shaped artifact that spreads through family group chats and community classes at zero CAC.
parsed.verdict_reason: Zero marginal cost keeps organic growth profitable, but the idea's own distribution target assumes 90% paid acquisition at $100-200 per payer against a $14-21 net lifetime value.
